bull.b: The Sobi agreement materially improves lacutamab’s development and commercialization pathway by providing a potential partner-led route into global markets. It also reduces reliance on Innate building a standalone sales infrastructure, subject to closing conditions and clinical success.

FDA clearance and multiple expedited designations strengthen lacutamab’s regulatory positioning in relapsed or refractory Sezary syndrome. These features can support more efficient development and potential accelerated approval, although the program still requires financing and successful trial execution.

The AstraZeneca collaboration provides exposure to multiple late-stage or advancing immunotherapy programs without requiring Innate to fund all development independently. Completed enrollment and substantial remaining milestone pools create durable non-product revenue potential if clinical and commercial targets are achieved.

bear.b: The limited runway creates a near-term financing dependency while several programs approach costly late-stage development. External funding, partnering or royalty financing may be required, increasing dilution, execution and timing risk if capital is not secured promptly.

Negative equity indicates that cumulative losses have materially eroded the balance sheet and reduced financial flexibility. Even with lower debt, the position can constrain financing options and heighten the likelihood of future dilution, refinancing pressure or dependence on strategic partners.

bear.t: High Burn and Weak Revenue Base
bear.b: Innate lacks recurring product revenue and remains far from self-funding, leaving operations dependent on grants, licensing proceeds and milestone timing. The large gap between income and spending makes earnings volatile and increases the financial consequences of clinical delays or unsuccessful programs.
